policy: A reviewed binding identifies exact C# and Java types plus tested behavior. Partial bindings cannot be counted as full parity.

KnownDifferences: C# Increment calls SourceClamp.Integer; Java Bits.inc clamps with local comparisons, so this C# call-graph edge has no corresponding Java call edge.
Java getDistanceD recursively calls itself; C# DistanceFraction computes a finite fraction.
Invalid set values throw different exception types; the numeric results are tested only for valid values.
CoreTimeCompat is an isolated engine-frame primitive; the Godot frame loop does not call it yet.
C# exposes a per-instance generator; Java RND uses one static global generator.
Other RND methods and their call-site ordering are not yet tested.

VerifiedMethods: Immigration.getImmigrants(Race) numerical branches via WantedUltimately(RaceRule,...), including threshold, zero population and camp capacity
KnownDifferences: The fixture isolates the Java source formula with explicit inputs; the original game class is not instantiated, so its runtime dependencies are not compared.
C# Update accumulates immigrationBoost * delta instead of Java speed(wanted) * ds with its seconds-per-day rate and camp branch.
C# does not subtract onTheirWay from non-camp wanted values and combines current population with incoming subjects in its call site.
C# clamps standingPower to at least 0.01 before division, unlike the Java source; fixture inputs have positive powers above this bound.
Java save/load, auto-admission, emigration, riot behavior and integration with world state are not covered.
